item.title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market — Sat Aug 15, 12:00 AM — Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
item.description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. item.title: Jeffrey Halford Duo — Sat Aug 15, 1:00 PM — Russian River Vineyards
item.description:
Of the many marks of genius associated with rock n’ roll greatness, the knack for surrounding oneself with transformational talent looms especially large, with The Rolling Stones being perhaps the most notable example. Jeffrey Halford treads a poetic rootsy path on his latest release, SOUL CRUSADE, combining a bulletproof collection of songs inspired by gospel, folk, soul, and blues, with a formidable roster of musical contributors. The result is one of Halford’s most approachable and easy-grooving.
His latest album release, SOUL CRUSADE, is the follow-up to the critically acclaimed record WEST TOWARDS SOUTH. The album came out in Europe on Continental Song City, debuted in September at \#2, and then undisputedly reached \#1 in October 2022 and stayed in the chart for four months.

item.title: The Great Other & Gas Money & One Armed Joey — Sat Aug 15, 7:00 PM — HopMonk Tavern
item.description:
The year was 2019. The Great Other blossomed to life by frontman Josh N. Wills, guitarist Zaid Johnson, bassist Nick Chavez, and drummer Emunti Herrera within the Oakland, California’s legendary music studio compound of Soundwave Studios.
Their inspiration gravitated towards the acts of Deftones, Meshuggah, Gojira, Tool, Alice in Chains, Opeth, Coheed and Cambria, and handfuls more across the musical spectrum, which has morphed them into a standout sound within the scene of East Bay hardcore, punk, and indie. They strive for each song, and each live performance to be a beautifully mind-altering, goosebump inducing, emotional rollercoaster of a journey.
Their debut demo release, “Nostalgia”, was let loose upon the world on August 8th, 2024 as the perfect unmasking of who they are, and what they are capable of. item.title: Sam Reider — Sun Aug 16, 11:30 AM — The Cotati Accordion Festival
item.description: SAM REIDER is a Latin GRAMMY-nominated pianist, accordionist, composer, and educator from San Francisco, California. His work brings together various streams of American music, from jazz and folk tunes to popular song and contemporary composition. He has appeared as a bandleader and soloist at major festivals and venues around the world and his performances and original compositions have been featured on NPR, PBS and the BBC. Reider has performed, recorded and collaborated with a range of artists including Jon Batiste, Jorge Glem, Sierra Hull, Laurie Lewis, and Paquito d’Rivera. From his genre-bending acoustic ensemble The Human Hands to his duo collaboration with Grammy-nominated Venezuelan artist Jorge Glem, Reider’s unique compositional voice and melodicism runs throughout his eclectic projects. item.title: Indestructible — Sun Aug 16, 3:00 PM — HEAD WEST Marketplace
item.description:
Former San Francisco private detective Donovan Plant spent nearly two decades chasing leads and tailing cheaters before returning to his musical roots. Donovan Plant blends rock, country and pop with lyrics inspired by the city.
Citing influences such as David Bowie, The Cars, and Jackson Brown, Donovan’s keen ear for hooks and melody is on full display with NIGHT FEEL GOOD, recorded inside the world-famous Hyde Street Studios at Dreamrack Studios by producer and engineer Trent Berry.
Donovan formed DONOVAN PLANT & THE LEAFS in 2018, a group that includes drummer Lliam Hart \(Information Society/Wire Train\), bassist Mike Henry \(Minus One\) and lead guitarist Jason Rojek \(Sugar Crash\). Lliam, Mike, and Jason have been playing live and recording together for years. item.title: Tlalok — Wed Aug 19, 8:00 PM — The Twisted Fisherman
item.description:
Tlalok is a bilingual singer/songwriter and multi-instrumentalist based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Originally a Chicago native, he comes from a long line of musicians dating back to his great-grandfather, a composer from Vicente Guerrero, Mexico. A century later, he keeps the family tradition alive through boleros, bossa novas, and vibrant performances channeling the passion of his ancestors.
In addition to his solo work, Tlalok leads and performs in a wide range of musical projects, from intimate jazz ensembles to large, high-energy dance bands spanning soul, disco, and Latin music.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Richard Turgeon — Wed Aug 19, 8:30 PM — HopMonk Tavern Novato
item.description:
Richard Turgeon is a San Francisco-based singer/songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and record producer. His alternative rock sound has been called "California Rock" or "New Vintage Rock," is regularly featured on SiriusXM, and has been featured in indie film soundtracks. He's currently playing live shows in the Bay Area and beyond with his trio, RT3.
Last year he played drums for national act Donnie Emerson, subject of the film "Dreamin' Wild," and Pavement co-founder Scott Kannberg recently shared Rich's cover/video of Pavement's song "Date with IKEA."
His critically acclaimed solo records from the last several years have made innumerable “best of” lists from various press outlets, radio stations and bloggers from around the world. Visit his website at www.richardturgeon.com

Vagabond Empire is an expansive new solo project for acoustic guitar, banjo, vocals, and whatever other sounds -- and guest players -- find their way into the mix.
Born from the ashes of critically acclaimed "bluevelvetgrass" string band Three Times Bad, Vagabond Empire's genre-expansive set list combines Americana classics with dynamic originals from three song collections: Singalongs for End Times, After the Plague, and American Sojourn.

item.title: Anthony Arya — Fri Aug 21, 6:00 PM — Civic Green
item.description:
Now 23 years old, Americana artist Anthony Arya’s skyrocketing career is taking him far beyond his roots in the San Francisco Bay Area. He burst onto the scene at just age 16, with his appearances on NBC’s The Voice. Since then, he has released four full-length albums winning national awards for his songwriting.
With his soulful lyrics and gritty guitar riffs, Arya brings the folk rock sound of Los Angeles’ Laurel Canyon into a modern era. In 2018, he released his debut album, Going To California, earning him the Presidential Scholar of the Arts in the Singer-Songwriter category. His second album, The Road, was inspired by the sensibilities of Bob Dylan, Beatnik writer Jack Kerouac and F. Scott Fitzgerald.
While attending university, Anthony produced Circles & the Flames - an album that would win him international attention for his songwriting including International Songwriting Competition Finalist, International Acoustic Music Awards Finalist, Bluebird Cafe Golden Pick Contest Win

item.title: Late for the Train — Fri Aug 21, 6:00 PM — Marinwood Community Center
item.description:
Late for the Train is a modern string band rooted in American folk and bluegrass music. Infused with the honest depth of the coastal redwood forests and the heartfelt community of the North Bay, the band provides a playful and poignant musical experience that uplifts the spirit and rouses the soul.
Travel back to a time of hearthside storytelling with these California natives, reveling in the rich traditions of Americana, bluegrass, folk, and Celtic music. Their dynamic songwriting is inspired by influences such as Emmylou Harris, Bob Dylan, Béla Fleck and Abigail Washburn, Mandolin Orange, Mipso, and Nickel Creek.
The core ensemble consists of songwriters and multi-instrumentalists David Pascoe \(guitar\), Laura Benson \(fiddle\), Thom Beneduci \(stand-up bass\), and Bud Dillard \(mandolin\).
